marta: heads-up — brought up a new reranker candidate (hybrid-rank-v1-int8). quick eval shows a surprising MRR drop on short queries, but long queries look stable. posting raw snippets below. :eyes:
omar: ugh, thanks. can you paste the eval command + sample sizes? is this from the ptq run or from qat baseline?
jenna: short note — last time we saw a similar pattern it was tied to candidate pooling + whitespace normalization collapsing ties. can you confirm candidate ordering before scoring?
marta: running eval with:
```bash
./eval_rerank.py --model hybrid-rank-v1-int8 --qset short-search-2026 --candidates 10 --seed 42 --metric mrr ndcg --bootstrap 200
```
this was PTQ (post-train quant) using our int8 kernel from the runtime pack.
sam: quick summary I grabbed from the run:
- baseline fp16 (hybrid-rank-v1-fp16): short MRR=0.318, long MRR=0.423
- int8 candidate: short MRR=0.279 (-12.3%), long MRR=0.419 (-0.9%)
- NDCG@10 nearly identical across both
liam: oof. is that drop outside bootstrap CI? what are the 95% bounds?
omar: please also try candidates=20 and candidates=5. if the drop scales with candidate pool that's a strong hint about tie-resolution or softmax temperature effects on tail scores.
marta: agreed — i'll run two ablations (candidates=5/20) and re-run with `--no-kvpack` (we suspect KV packing/prefix caching interaction).
jena: also check tokenizer parity between the offline eval pipeline and runtime: tokenizer config differences (strip_accents, collapse_whitespace) can change snippet lengths and lead to different attention masks. i remember we changed `tokenizer.normalizer = True` on the hf release.
sam: small debug patch you can run:
```python
# sample compare
from hf_tokenizers import Tokenizer
base = Tokenizer.from_pretrained('hybrid/v1/tokenizer')
prod = Tokenizer.from_pretrained('hub/flan-3b-tokenizer')
print(base.encode('example query').tokens, prod.encode('example query').tokens)
```
this quickly shows if tokenization drift exists.
infra-bot: deploy hyb-rank-int8 -> staging completed (gpu-pool-4) :white_check_mark:
liam: when you have the new ablation numbers, please include bootstrap CIs. we need to know if this is a real quality regression or just sample noise. also add per-query-length buckets (<=6, 7-15, >15) so we can see where mass loss occurs.
omar: if ablations point to KV packing, we should also test with `--pad-left` vs `--pad-right` because cache alignment changes can affect KV reuse and quant rounding.
marta: thanks — i'm kicking off ablation runs now (candidates 5/20, no-kvpack, pad-left/right, tokenizer parity). will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
sam: if you want faster signal, run a smaller bootstrap (50) across 3 different seeds to get variance estimate in ~10min.
jena: and include a tiny deterministic probe: the top-5 candidate ordering for 20 hand-picked short queries so we can inspect tie-breaks manually.
marta: noted — will attach the probe list and top-5 diffs after runs. thanks all.
omar: also file a quick eval ticket so we don't lose experiment config: EVAL-4623 (link: https://go/reports/EVAL-4623)
marta: filed and linked to thread.
